input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages—those MMS things—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough—do you need my date of birth too?

I see that my phone shows a poor signal and it says "2G" at the top. I think I can make regular calls and send normal texts, but I’m not sure about browsing the internet with mobile data. Is there a simple way to check that? Also, does the "2G" thing matter for sending picture messages?
Okay, I changed the setting to prefer 4G and 5G, and now the top of my phone shows "5G" with excellent signal. What should I do next? Should I try sending a picture message again now?
I just tried to send a picture message, but it still won’t go through. It’s still not working, even though the signal looks much better now. What should I do next?
I tried checking my internet connection with mobile data, but it looks like there’s no connection at all. Does this mean my mobile data isn’t working? What should I do now?

My mobile data is already turned on, and Wi-Fi is off. The phone says it’s connected to 5G with excellent signal, but I still can’t get on the internet. What should I try next? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I lose anything important if we keep trying things?

I found something called "APN" in my phone’s settings, and it says the APN name is "internet" and there’s a web address listed for picture messages. I don’t see any error messages. Is this how it’s supposed to look, or do I need to change something here? I’m not sure what any of this means.
If you’re sure it won’t erase my photos or anything important, then yes, I’m okay with resetting the APN settings to default. What do I need to do?

I found the option and reset the APN settings like you said. It says the settings will reset when I restart my phone. I’m a bit nervous about rebooting—are you sure I won’t lose my photos or anything else important if I do this?
I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t use mobile data or send picture messages. It’s really frustrating—nothing seems to be working. Is there anything else we can try?
Oh, I see. That explains it! I’d like to add 2GB of data, please. Can you tell me the total price before you go ahead? I just want to make sure I understand.
Yes, please go ahead and add the 2GB for $4.00. I really want to be able to send pictures again. Let me know when it’s done and what I should do next!

I restarted my phone again, but I still can’t use mobile data or send picture messages. It’s still not working, even after adding the extra data. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get really worried this won’t ever work again.
Yes, please transfer me to a human agent. I really need this fixed, and I’m feeling a bit overwhelmed. Thank you for your help so far.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

- The phone number associated with your account,

Thank you for providing your phone number. I have identified your account. To help you fix the MMS (picture messaging) issue, I’ll need to guide you through a few quick checks and steps on your phone.

First, can you confirm:
- Are you able to make regular calls and send/receive regular text messages (SMS)?
- Are you able to browse the internet using mobile data (not Wi-Fi)?

This will help me determine if the issue is specific to MMS or related to your general service or data connection.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I see that my phone shows a poor signal and it says "2G" at the top. I think I can make regular calls and send normal texts, but I’m not sure about browsing the internet with mobile data. Is there a simple way to check that? Also, does the "2G" thing matter for sending picture messages?

Thank you for the details. Yes, the "2G" network can be a problem for sending picture messages (MMS). MMS requires at least a 3G, 4G, or 5G connection—2G is generally not suitable for sending or receiving MMS.

Let’s try to improve your network connection by switching your phone’s network mode to prefer 4G or 5G, if available. On your phone, please look for the option to change your network mode and select “4G/5G preferred” or “4G only.” 

After you do this, check if your signal improves and if the network indicator changes from "2G" to "3G," "4G," or "5G." Once you’ve done that, try sending a picture message again.

If you need step-by-step instructions for changing the network mode, please let me know your phone’s make and model, and I can guide you further.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I changed the setting to prefer 4G and 5G, and now the top of my phone shows "5G" with excellent signal. What should I do next? Should I try sending a picture message again now?

Great job updating your network settings! Now that your phone is connected to "5G" with excellent signal, please try sending a picture message (MMS) again.

Let me know if it goes through successfully or if you still experience any issues. If it still doesn’t work, I’ll guide you through the next troubleshooting steps.

Thank you for letting me know. Since your signal is now excellent and you’re on 5G, let’s check if your mobile data is working, as MMS requires an active mobile data connection.

Can you try opening a website or using an app that needs internet (with Wi-Fi turned off) to see if you have internet access through mobile data? Let me know if you’re able to browse the web or if you get any errors. This will help us determine if the issue is with mobile data or something else.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried checking my internet connection with mobile data, but it looks like there’s no connection at all. Does this mean my mobile data isn’t working? What should I do now?

Thank you for checking. Since your mobile data isn’t working, that could be the reason why MMS isn’t going through. Let’s troubleshoot your mobile data connection.

First, please check if mobile data is enabled on your phone. Make sure Wi-Fi is turned off, then look for a setting called “Mobile Data” or “Cellular Data” and ensure it is switched ON.

After turning on mobile data, try browsing the internet again. Let me know if you’re able to connect, or if you still have no internet access. If it’s already on and still not working, please let me know so we can try the next step.

My mobile data is already turned on, and Wi-Fi is off. The phone says it’s connected to 5G with excellent signal, but I still can’t get on the internet. What should I try next? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I lose anything important if we keep trying things?

Thank you for your patience. You won’t lose any personal data or important information by following these troubleshooting steps. The actions we’ll try are safe and commonly used to fix mobile data issues.

Next, let’s check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings can prevent mobile data and MMS from working. Please look for a setting called “Access Point Names” or “APN” in your phone’s network or cellular settings and check if anything looks unusual or if there are any error messages.

If you’re not sure how to check this, let me know your phone’s make and model, and I can guide you step by step. If you see an option to “Reset to default” or “Reset APN settings,” please let me know before proceeding, and I’ll confirm the next steps for you.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I found something called "APN" in my phone’s settings, and it says the APN name is "internet" and there’s a web address listed for picture messages. I don’t see any error messages. Is this how it’s supposed to look, or do I need to change something here? I’m not sure what any of this means.

Thank you for checking your APN settings. Since there’s an APN name and a web address listed for picture messages (MMSC), and no error messages, your settings might be correct. However, sometimes these settings can still become misconfigured, which can cause issues with mobile data and MMS.

To be sure, the next safe step is to reset your APN settings to default. This will not erase any of your personal data—just the network settings, which will be restored to the correct values for your carrier.

Would you like to proceed with resetting your APN settings to default? If so, please confirm, and I’ll guide you through the process and let you know what to do next.
If you’re sure it won’t erase my photos or anything important, then yes, I’m okay with resetting the APN settings to default. What do I need to do?

Thank you for your confirmation. Resetting your APN settings will not erase your photos, messages, or any personal data—it only restores your network settings to the default values needed for your carrier.

Please follow these steps:
1. In your phone’s APN settings, look for an option that says “Reset to default” or “Reset APN settings.”
2. Select that option and confirm if prompted.

After you reset the APN settings, you’ll need to restart (reboot) your phone for the changes to take effect. Once your phone restarts, try using mobile data and sending a picture message again.

Let me know once you’ve completed these steps, or if you need help finding the reset option.

APN settings will reset at reboot.

I found the option and reset the APN settings like you said. It says the settings will reset when I restart my phone. I’m a bit nervous about rebooting—are you sure I won’t lose my photos or anything else important if I do this?

You will not lose your photos, messages, contacts, or any other personal data by restarting (rebooting) your phone. Restarting simply turns your phone off and back on, which is a safe and common troubleshooting step.

Please go ahead and restart your phone now. Once it’s back on, try using mobile data and sending a picture message again. Let me know how it goes or if you need any further help.
